title: No Brain. Yet a Touch Can Leave a Fading Memory.
description:
A Venus flytrap has no brain. A brief stimulus can still leave information behind in the leaf. Watch how a recent signal can build on that fading response—and why a longer delay changes the outcome.

“Memory” here means a temporary biochemical state, not conscious recollection. Touches, electrical signals and calcium changes are different; responses depend on stimulus and timing.

AI-generated botanical illustrations and synthetic narration. Calcium marks and signal timing are schematic, not naturally visible fluorescence or measured cellular activity. Research clips are cropped/enlarged excerpts with source slow motion and a held ending where indicated. Closure footage shows a separate specimen.

Research: Suda et al. (2020): https://doi.org/10.1038/s41477-020-00773-1
Footage: Burri et al. (2020), S1/S2, CC BY 4.0: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pbio.3000740 | https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
Closure: Poppinga et al. (2016), S4, CC BY 2.0: https://doi.org/10.3762/bjnano.7.59 | https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/
